docs.title: vexy-subs
docs.text:
vexy-subs generates subtitles for a video on your own machine, with one colour per speaker. It recognises the words, works out who said each one, restores sentence punctuation, cleans up hesitations and lays the text out as readable captions. You can give it the names and terms used in the recording so that they are recognised and spelled correctly.

vexy-subs transcribe clip.mp4 --prompt_file=hints.md --output_dir=subtitles

For clip.mp4, this writes five files into subtitles/:

File Contents clip.ass captions with a named, coloured style per speaker clip.vtt WebVTT with voice spans, cue classes and CSS colour rules clip.srt SubRip with <font color> tags clip.words.json every recognised word with its times and speaker clip.vexy-subs.json a receipt with settings, hashes and checks

The recognition, diarization and punctuation models run locally on Apple Silicon. No API key is needed. Only translate, and the optional LLM route of the caption clean-up, send text to an endpoint that you configure.

docs.title: What it can do
docs.text:
• Transcribe a video or a folder of videos into speaker-coloured subtitles. See Transcription.
  • Beautify existing captions: remove fillers, balance lines and fix timing, without repeating recognition. See Beautification.
  • Translate SRT, VTT, ASS or SSA files with any OpenAI-compatible model, keeping every cue's timing and the ASS speaker styles. See Translation.
  • Verify a folder of results against their receipts. See Command reference.

docs.title: How a video becomes subtitles
docs.text:
1. FFmpeg decodes the audio.
  2. MLX Whisper recognises timed words, using your hints as context.
  3. Collapsed word timestamps are repaired with a forced aligner.
  4. A diarizer finds who speaks when across the whole recording.
  5. Each word is assigned to the speaker active at that time.
  6. A punctuation model adds one punctuation label per word.
  7. Beautification detects the language, removes disfluencies, and builds balanced, well-timed cues.
  8. The cues are written as ASS, WebVTT and SRT, then parsed again and checked.

Each model stage saves its result in a .work folder, so a failed run can resume without repeating the stages that succeeded.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The vexy_subs package exports the subtitle translation API, which is compatible with the retired vttrix package.

from vexy_subs import load_subtitles, save_subtitles, translate_subtitles_sync

subs = load_subtitles("talk.srt")
save_subtitles(translate_subtitles_sync(subs, "cerebras-code", "en", "pl"), "talk.pl.vtt")

This loads talk.srt, translates it with the cerebras-code profile from config.toml, and saves the result as WebVTT.

docs.title: Exports
docs.text: Name Kind Subtitle data class for one cue SubtitleFile data class for a parsed file load_subtitles function save_subtitles function translate_subtitles coroutine function translate_subtitles_sync function __version__ string

docs.title: Subtitle
docs.text:
@dataclass
class Subtitle:
    start_ms: int
    end_ms: int
    text: str

Times are whole milliseconds, which avoids floating-point drift. text is plain text with \n between lines.

docs.title: SubtitleFile
docs.text:
@dataclass
class SubtitleFile:
    events: list[Subtitle]
    format: str = "srt"
    source_path: str | None = None
    ssa: pysubs2.SSAFile | None = None
    recognized: bool = True

ssa keeps the original parsed file so that styles survive a save. recognized is False when the file could not be parsed as subtitles.

docs.title: load_subtitles(path)
docs.text: Loads an SRT, VTT, ASS or SSA file and returns a SubtitleFile. Comment events are dropped. An empty or unrecognisable file loads with no cues and recognized=False.

docs.title: save_subtitles(subtitle_file, path, fmt=None)
docs.text:
Writes the cues to path. The format is fmt if given, otherwise taken from the extension of path (.srt, .vtt, .ass or .ssa), otherwise the file's own format.

If the file came from load_subtitles and still has the same number of cues, its styles and the per-cue style and speaker fields are kept by position; only times and text change. After you reorder or replace cues, set ssa=None so that styles are not applied to the wrong cues.

Text in braces, {...}, is read as an ASS override tag and is lost.

docs.title: translate_subtitles_sync(subtitle_file, llm_spec, source_lang, target_lang, vocab_path=None)
docs.text:
Translates every cue and returns a new SubtitleFile with the same timing and the same ssa styles.

  • llm_spec is a profile name, model::ENV_KEY::base_url, or a comma-separated fallback list. See Configuration.
  • vocab_path names an optional JSON glossary.

The translation follows the process described in Translation.

docs.title: translate_subtitles(...)
docs.text:
The awaitable form of translate_subtitles_sync, with the same arguments. The blocking HTTP calls run in a worker thread.

import asyncio
from vexy_subs import load_subtitles, save_subtitles, translate_subtitles

async def main() -> None:
    subs = load_subtitles("talk.ass")
    result = await translate_subtitles(subs, "fast,careful", "English", "German")
    save_subtitles(result, "talk.de.ass")

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Beautification
docs.text:
Beautification turns timed words into captions that are easier to read. It runs by default in transcribe, batch and render. Add --beautify=False to get the plain, verbatim layout instead.

The beautify command applies the same clean-up to subtitles you already have, without repeating recognition, diarization or punctuation.

docs.title: What it changes
docs.text:
1. Language. langid's bundled 97-language model detects the language from a sample across the whole recording. --language (or --beautify_language in the integrated commands) overrides it, which helps for short or mixed-language recordings.
  2. Disfluencies. Hesitation tokens such as uhm, err, ähm and euh are removed. Accidental restarts next to each other within one speaker turn are collapsed. English padding such as hedging kind of, basically, and marked you know or I mean is removed. Literal uses such as a special kind of font, works well and what you know are kept, as are deliberate emphasis, negation, valid repeats such as had had or that that, names and numbers.
  3. Sentences. Sentence capitalisation and the punctuation of standalone responses are repaired.
  4. Typography. Unicode normalisation, curly apostrophes, ellipses and the language's quotation marks are applied across the text as a whole, not line by line. French gets non-breaking spaces before punctuation.
  5. Cue boundaries. Dynamic programming chooses where cues break. It strongly penalises short cues and fast reading speeds. For English, a part-of-speech tagger keeps articles with their nouns, pronouns with their verbs, auxiliaries and names together. Other languages use explicit grammatical boundary rules.
  6. Line balance. Pillow measures real font advances, preferring an installed Arial, so each two-line cue is optically balanced and avoids orphan lines.
  7. Timing. Cues are retimed to the frame grid, as described below.

Every deletion is recorded in the receipt with its original text, times and reason. These are grammatical predictions, not a guarantee of perfect editorial phrasing.

docs.title: Timing rules
docs.text:
The frame rate comes from the video next to the subtitles when there is one. Otherwise it is 25 fps; --fps overrides it.

Rule Value Start snapping within one frame End extension up to 0.5 seconds of free space Minimum duration 5/6 second Maximum duration 7 seconds Gap between cues two frames, or at least half a second Line length 42 characters, at most two lines

Reading speed targets, in visible characters per second:

Language Characters per second English 20 German, French, Polish 17 Other languages 17 (unverified fallback)

Formatting tags do not count towards these lengths. Long single words and fast speaker changes can make some rules impossible to meet without changing the meaning; such cues are kept and reported.

docs.title: The audit
docs.text:
The receipt holds beautification.audit. Its violations list names every cue that still breaks a numeric rule. With --strict, a set with unresolved violations is not written.

Passing the numeric checks does not certify a delivery for a streaming platform. Shot changes, dialogue sync, glyph coverage, regional editorial rules and playback still need review. The rules are based on the Netflix timed-text style guides (general requirements, timing, English, German, French and Polish), but the speaker colours are a project convention, not Netflix's white-text delivery style.

docs.title: Beautify existing subtitles
docs.text:
beautify accepts a folder, an SRT, WebVTT or ASS file, a .words.json file or a .vexy-subs.json receipt.

# Every subtitle set under a folder tree, local route only
vexy-subs beautify /path/to/videos --recursive --backend=local

# Timed words, with the language and frame rate given
vexy-subs beautify talk.words.json --language=en --fps=25

# Write cleaned files to another folder
vexy-subs beautify captions.srt --output_dir=cleaned

# Refuse to replace a set that still has violations
vexy-subs beautify captions.ass --strict

What happens to the files:

  • By default the set is replaced in place. The original captions, timed words and receipt are saved once in <stem>.work/beautify-original/.
  • --output_dir writes the result elsewhere and leaves the originals alone.
  • A repeat run with the same settings checks the hashes and skips.
  • --force processes again from the saved originals, so edits never pile up.
  • With --recursive, folders named private, .venv, .git, beautify-original and any .work folder are skipped.
  • --verbose adds debug detail on the error stream.

When the input is a caption file without timed words, word times are estimated in proportion to the text. The receipt marks them as estimates. Original word times are always used when they are available.

docs.title: Local and LLM routes
docs.text:
The local route uses only bundled or cached models. Caption text stays on your machine.

The LLM route sends batches of caption words with anonymous speaker IDs to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The model may delete unnecessary words and fix casing and punctuation. Its reply is rejected if it inserts or reorders words, rewrites a word, deletes a number or an acronym, or deletes more than 30% of a batch. Timestamps and speaker IDs never leave your machine and are never changed by the model. API keys never appear in receipts or on standard output.

The route is chosen by --backend (beautify) or --beautify_backend (transcribe, batch, render):

Value Route local always local llm always the LLM; fails if no model is configured auto (default) the LLM when a model is configured, otherwise local

Configuration explains how to configure the model.

• Added translate, ported from the retired vttrix package: two-pass (translate, refine) LLM subtitle translation for SRT, VTT, ASS and SSA, with a JSON glossary and the previous chunk as context. Timing and ASS speaker styles are kept, and the output format follows the destination extension. Cues travel as numbered JSON; a dropped, merged or reordered cue is retried and then fails, instead of shifting timestamps.
  • Added Codex-style [model_providers.*] and [profiles.*] configuration, provider discovery from {PREFIX}_API_KEY with {PREFIX}_API_ENDPOINT or _API_OPENAI, model::ENV_KEY::base_url specs, comma-separated fallback lists, and the llm command group (path, profiles, discover --save, check).
  • Beautification can pick its LLM by spec: --llm, VEXY_SUBS_LLM or [llm] profile.
  • Exported the vttrix library API: Subtitle, SubtitleFile, load_subtitles, save_subtitles, translate_subtitles, translate_subtitles_sync. A missing --vocab file is now an error.

• Added build.sh and publish.sh.
  • Versions come from git tags through hatch-vcs. Added a version command.
  • Remove unnecessary English discourse phrases such as hedging kind of, marked you know/I mean, and repeated phrase starts, while protecting literal uses, complete responses, names, numbers and meaningful emphasis.
  • Normalise English sentence capitalisation and standalone response punctuation.
  • Added automatic and standalone subtitle beautification with language detection.
  • Added grammatical and measured-font line balancing, frame-aware retiming, filler and restart removal, and language-specific Unicode typography.
  • Added optional validated LLM editing configured through dotenv, environment variables or TOML, keeping credentials out of receipts.
  • Added original-caption backups, repeat-run hash checks and numeric caption-rule audits with strict refusal.

• Added speaker-coloured ASS, styled WebVTT and coloured SRT exports.
  • Added continuous diarization and speaker-aware cue segmentation.
  • Added punctuation restoration that preserves timed words.
  • Added UTF-8 Markdown and text hint files passed to Whisper.
  • Added the Fire command-line tool, resumable model stages and hash verification.

The full history is in CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
vexy-subs is a Fire command-line tool. Flags use underscores, as in --output_dir, and Boolean flags take an explicit value, as in --beautify=False. Results are printed as JSON on standard output; progress goes to standard error. Add --help after a command to print its flags:

vexy-subs transcribe --help
Command Purpose transcribe make subtitles for one video batch make subtitles for every matching video in a folder render render edited timed words without any model beautify clean up existing subtitles translate translate a subtitle file with an LLM verify check completed subtitle sets against their receipts llm manage LLM providers and profiles doctor report local prerequisites version print the installed package version

docs.title: transcribe
docs.text:
vexy-subs transcribe VIDEO [flags]
Flag Default Meaning --output_dir the video's folder where outputs and the .work folder go --prompt_file empty UTF-8 .md or .txt hint file --prompt empty inline hints --language en recognition language; "" detects it --asr_model mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo Whisper model --diar_model mlx-community/Nemotron-3-Diarization-8bit Nemotron diarization model --punctuation_model oliverguhr/fullstop-punctuation-multilang-large punctuation model --alignment_model mlx-community/Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B-8bit forced aligner for timestamp repair --diar_backend auto auto, nemotron or cluster --turns_file empty verified speaker turns instead of diarization --max_speakers 40 upper limit for cluster --speaker_map empty JSON object mapping speaker IDs to names --force False regenerate existing outputs --beautify True apply beautification --beautify_backend from configuration local, llm or auto --beautify_language detected language for beautification --config_file platform config file config.toml to use --env_file empty .env file to load --llm empty LLM spec for beautification --fps 0 frame rate; 0 reads it from the video --strict False fail if numeric caption rules are not met

See Transcription.

docs.title: batch
docs.text:
vexy-subs batch [FOLDER] [flags]

FOLDER defaults to the current folder.

Flag Default Meaning --output_dir each video's folder where outputs go --prompt_dir empty folder with one <stem>.md or <stem>.txt per video --pattern *.mp4 which files to process --force False regenerate existing outputs --language en recognition language --diar_backend auto diarization back-end --max_speakers 40 upper limit for cluster --beautify True apply beautification --beautify_backend from configuration local, llm or auto --beautify_language detected language for beautification --config_file, --env_file, --llm empty as for transcribe --strict False fail if numeric caption rules are not met --fps 0 frame rate; 0 reads it from each video

Each video runs in its own process. Failures are collected and reported at the end as an error that lists the failed file names.

docs.title: render
docs.text:
vexy-subs render WORDS_FILE OUTPUT_STEM [flags]

Renders a .words.json file to OUTPUT_STEM.ass, .vtt and .srt without loading any model. Use it after you edit the words by hand.

Flag Default Meaning --speaker_map empty JSON object mapping speaker IDs to names --force False replace existing caption files --beautify True apply beautification --language detected language for beautification --fps 25 frame rate --backend from configuration local, llm or auto --config_file, --env_file, --llm empty as for transcribe

docs.title: beautify
docs.text:
vexy-subs beautify [PATH] [flags]

PATH is a folder, an SRT, WebVTT or ASS file, a .words.json file or a .vexy-subs.json receipt. It defaults to the current folder.

Flag Default Meaning --language detected language --fps 0 frame rate; 0 reads it from a neighbouring video, else 25 --backend from configuration local, llm or auto --config_file, --env_file, --llm empty as for transcribe --recursive False search subfolders --output_dir empty write results here instead of replacing in place --force False reprocess from the saved originals --strict False do not replace a set with unresolved violations --verbose False debug output on standard error

See Beautification.

docs.title: translate
docs.text:
vexy-subs translate SRC DST LLM SOURCE_LANG TARGET_LANG [flags]
Flag Default Meaning --vocab empty JSON glossary of exact term translations --config_file platform config file config.toml to use --env_file empty .env file to load --chunk_size 40 cues per request --refine True run the refining pass --timeout 60 seconds per request --force False replace an existing output

See Translation.

docs.title: verify
docs.text:
vexy-subs verify [FOLDER] [flags]

Checks every *.vexy-subs.json receipt in FOLDER (default: the current folder).

Flag Default Meaning --source_dir empty folder with the source videos --pattern *.mp4 which source files to expect --strict False fail on unresolved caption rule violations

For each set, verify:

  1. compares the hash of each output with the receipt,
  2. parses the SRT, ASS and WebVTT files and checks cue counts, text, timeline and speaker styling,
  3. checks that the captions contain every character of the timed words,
  4. reruns the numeric caption audit and reports numeric_violations.

With --source_dir, it also checks each source video's hash and fails if a matching video has no subtitles. Without it, only the completed sets are checked. A folder with no completed set is an error.

docs.title: llm
docs.text:
vexy-subs llm path
vexy-subs llm profiles [--config_file=FILE] [--env_file=FILE]
vexy-subs llm discover [--save] [--config_file=FILE] [--env_file=FILE]
vexy-subs llm check SPEC [--config_file=FILE] [--env_file=FILE]

See Configuration.

docs.title: doctor
docs.text:
vexy-subs doctor

Prints the version, platform, architecture, whether ffmpeg and ffprobe are on PATH, and whether the apple and cluster extras are installed.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
vexy-subs version

Prints the installed package version.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Configuration controls the beautification route, the optional LLM, and the LLM providers and profiles used by translate. Recognition and diarization take their settings from command-line flags only.

docs.title: Where settings come from
docs.text:
For each setting, the first source that provides it wins:

  1. an explicit command-line flag,
  2. an environment variable, including variables loaded from .env files,
  3. config.toml,
  4. the built-in default.

docs.title: config.toml
docs.text:
The file is config.toml in the platform's user configuration folder for vexy-subs. On macOS this is:

~/Library/Application Support/vexy-subs/config.toml

Linux uses the XDG configuration folder, and Windows the user's local application-data folder. Print the exact path with:

vexy-subs llm path

--config_file uses another file; that file must exist.

docs.title: .env files
docs.text:
python-dotenv loads, in this order, without overriding variables that are already set:

  1. the file given with --env_file, or else a .env found from the working folder,
  2. the .env file next to config.toml.

Keep API keys in the environment or a private .env file. config.toml stores only the names of key variables.

docs.title: Beautification and LLM settings
docs.text:
[beautify]
backend = "auto" # local, llm, or auto: llm only when a model is configured
# font = "/absolute/path/to/Arial.ttf"

[llm]
model = "your-loaded-model"
base_url = "http://localhost:1234/v1" # OpenAI-compatible chat completions
api_key_env = "VEXY_SUBS_LLM_API_KEY"
timeout = 60
Setting Environment variable Default [beautify] backend VEXY_SUBS_BEAUTIFY_BACKEND auto [beautify] font VEXY_SUBS_FONT installed Arial [llm] model VEXY_SUBS_LLM_MODEL none [llm] base_url VEXY_SUBS_LLM_BASE_URL http://localhost:1234/v1 [llm] api_key_env — OPENAI_API_KEY API key value VEXY_SUBS_LLM_API_KEY the variable named by api_key_env [llm] timeout VEXY_SUBS_LLM_TIMEOUT 60 seconds [llm] profile VEXY_SUBS_LLM none

With backend = "auto", the LLM route is used only when a model is configured. The LLM route needs a model and an http:// or https:// base URL. The timeout must be a positive number.

The flags for these settings differ by command:

Command Route flag Language flag beautify --backend --language transcribe, batch --beautify_backend --beautify_language render --backend --language

All of them accept --config_file, --env_file and --llm.

docs.title: LLM providers and profiles
docs.text:
Providers and profiles use the Codex CLI layout, in the same config.toml:

[model_providers.cerebras]
base_url = "https://api.cerebras.ai/v1"
env_key = "CEREBRAS_API_KEY"

[profiles.cerebras-code]
model = "zai-glm-4.7"
model_provider = "cerebras"

A provider names an endpoint and the environment variable that holds its key. A profile names a model and a provider.

docs.title: LLM specs
docs.text:
Wherever a command takes an LLM, you can give:

Spec Example a profile name cerebras-code an explicit spec, model::ENV_KEY::base_url gpt-4o::OPENAI_API_KEY::https://api.openai.com/v1 a comma-separated fallback list fast,careful

translate takes the spec as a positional argument. transcribe, render, batch and beautify take it as --llm. It can also come from VEXY_SUBS_LLM or [llm] profile. A spec replaces the [llm] model, base URL and key. Beautification uses only the first entry of a list. VEXY_SUBS_LLM_MODEL and VEXY_SUBS_LLM_BASE_URL still take precedence over a [llm] profile in the file. The local route never resolves a spec.

Name profiles with letters. Fire, the command-line library, turns values such as 1e3 or true into numbers or Booleans before vexy-subs sees them.

docs.title: Discovered providers
docs.text: A provider is also discovered from the environment when an upper-case {PREFIX}_API_KEY variable is paired with {PREFIX}_API_ENDPOINT or {PREFIX}_API_OPENAI holding an HTTP(S) URL. For example, GROQ_API_KEY and GROQ_API_ENDPOINT give a provider named groq. A provider in config.toml replaces a discovered one with the same name.

docs.title: The llm commands
docs.text:
Command Effect vexy-subs llm path print the location of config.toml vexy-subs llm profiles list profiles and providers, configured and discovered, and whether each key is set vexy-subs llm discover list discovered providers vexy-subs llm discover --save append discovered providers to config.toml, keeping existing text and comments vexy-subs llm check SPEC resolve a spec without calling the model

None of these commands prints a key value. discover --save adds only providers that are not already in the file, and refuses to write a file that would not parse.

Check a spec before a long run:

vexy-subs llm check cerebras-code

The output lists the resolved model, base URL, key variable name and whether the key is set.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-subs.git
cd vexy-subs

  2. Run the tests. uv creates the environment with the test extra:

    ./test.sh

    test.sh runs pytest with coverage of vexy_subs and fails below 80% coverage. It then runs ruff check on src and tests.

The tests use synthetic fixtures only. They do not need the apple extra.

docs.title: Source layout
docs.text: Module Responsibility cli.py Fire commands: render, batch, verify, doctor, llm pipeline.py the transcribe pipeline and its resumable stages inference.py MLX Whisper recognition and diarization alignment.py timestamp repair with a forced aligner punctuation.py punctuation restoration speakers.py assigning words to speakers hints.py reading hint files and Names:/Terms: vocabulary cues.py the plain cue layout used with --beautify=False beautify.py, editorial.py, typography.py, layout.py, syntax.py beautification beautify_config.py, beautify_llm.py beautification settings and the LLM route postprocess.py the beautify command formats.py writing and checking ASS, WebVTT and SRT translate.py the translate command and the Python API llm.py providers, profiles, specs and validated JSON chat calls io.py, types.py decoding, hashing, stage caching and data classes

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
./build.sh            # documentation and package
./build.sh docs       # documentation only
./build.sh package    # package only

The package step removes dist/, runs uv build and checks the result with twine check. The version comes from the git tag through hatch-vcs and is written to src/vexy_subs/__version__.py, which git ignores. An untagged commit builds a development version, which PyPI does not accept.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation source is in src_docs/md/, and src_docs/mkdocs.yml configures ProperDocs with the MaterialX theme:

src_docs/build.sh          # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

GitHub Pages serves docs/ at https://vexy.dev/vexy-subs/. A push to main that changes src_docs/ rebuilds docs/ through the Docs workflow.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
./publish.sh

publish.sh runs uvx gitnextver, which commits pending changes, creates the next vX.Y.Z tag and pushes. It stops if HEAD then carries no such tag. It then builds the package from that tag and uploads it with uv publish. A credential such as UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN must be set.

Run ./test.sh before you publish; publish.sh does not run the tests.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: MLX Whisper, Nemotron diarization, FullStop punctuation, CPU diarization, WebVTT.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or later.
  • uv to install the command-line tool.
  • For transcription: a Mac with Apple Silicon, and FFmpeg with ffprobe on PATH.

The base package installs without any inference library. It can beautify, translate, render and verify subtitles on any platform that runs Python 3.12.

docs.title: Choose the extras
docs.text: Extra Installs Needed for apple mlx-whisper, mlx-audio, deepmultilingualpunctuation, torch, transformers, soundfile transcribe and batch cluster diarize CPU speaker clustering for recordings with more than eight speakers test pytest, pytest-cov, ruff, build, twine development

docs.title: Install the tool
docs.text:
1. Install the package with the extras you need. For local transcription with both diarization back-ends:

    uv tool install 'vexy-subs[apple,cluster]'

    To install from a source checkout instead, run this in the repository folder:

    uv tool install './[apple,cluster]'

    For beautification, translation and rendering only, the base package is enough:

    uv tool install vexy-subs

  2. Check the installation:

    vexy-subs doctor

    The command prints JSON like this:

    {
  "version": "1.0.1",
  "auth_required": false,
  "platform": "Darwin",
  "architecture": "arm64",
  "ffmpeg": true,
  "ffprobe": true,
  "inference_installed": true,
  "cluster_installed": true
}

    inference_installed is true when mlx_whisper, mlx_audio and deepmultilingualpunctuation can be imported. cluster_installed is true when the diarize package is installed.

docs.title: Model downloads
docs.text:
The first transcription downloads open model weights from Hugging Face:

Stage Default model Speech recognition mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo Diarization mlx-community/Nemotron-3-Diarization-8bit Punctuation oliverguhr/fullstop-punctuation-multilang-large Timestamp repair mlx-community/Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B-8bit

The forced aligner is loaded only when a recording has collapsed or out-of-order word timestamps. Each model can be replaced with a flag; see Command reference.

For English, beautification also uses NLTK's small averaged-perceptron part-of-speech tagger. Its weights download once into the user cache folder.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This walk-through makes subtitles for a talk, talk.mp4, in which the speakers mention the product names QuasarAPI and OpenType.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• vexy-subs is installed with the apple extra, and vexy-subs doctor reports "inference_installed": true. See Installation.
  • ffmpeg and ffprobe are on PATH.

docs.title: Make subtitles for one video
docs.text:
1. Write a hint file, talk.md, with the names and terms used in the talk:

    Terms: QuasarAPI, OpenType, Python.
This talk discusses font shaping. Preserve the terminology when it is spoken.

    The terms on the Terms: line are sent to Whisper as recognition context, and keep their casing when punctuation is restored.

  2. Run transcribe:

    vexy-subs transcribe talk.mp4 --prompt_file=talk.md --output_dir=subtitles

    Progress goes to the terminal's error stream:

    ASR talk.mp4
DIARIZATION talk.mp4
PUNCTUATION talk.mp4
DONE talk.mp4: 212 cues, 2 speakers

    The receipt is printed as JSON on standard output.

  3. Open subtitles/talk.ass in a desktop player such as mpv or VLC, next to the video. Each speaker has their own colour.

The result is five files in subtitles/: talk.ass, talk.vtt, talk.srt, talk.words.json and talk.vexy-subs.json. The model results are kept in subtitles/talk.work/.

docs.title: Name the speakers
docs.text:
Speaker IDs are anonymous, such as speaker_0. Once you have checked who each speaker is, you can show names instead.

  1. Write labels.json:

    {"speaker_0": "Presenter", "speaker_1": "Guest"}

  2. Render the existing timed words with the map, under a new name:

    vexy-subs render subtitles/talk.words.json subtitles/talk.named \
  --speaker_map=labels.json

    This writes subtitles/talk.named.ass, .vtt and .srt without running any model. Keep the new name: overwriting talk.ass would no longer match the hashes in talk.vexy-subs.json, and verify would fail.

To have names from the start, pass --speaker_map to transcribe. The map is part of the run settings, so changing it later with transcribe --force runs every model stage again.

docs.title: Correct the words and render again
docs.text:
If a word is wrong, edit the timed words and render them without any model.

  1. Copy subtitles/talk.words.json to edited.words.json and correct the text of the wrong words.

  2. Render the edited words:

    vexy-subs render edited.words.json subtitles/edited

    This writes subtitles/edited.ass, .vtt and .srt.

docs.title: Process a folder of videos
docs.text:
1. Put one hint file per video in hints/, named after the video: hints/talk.md for videos/talk.mp4.

  2. Run batch:

    vexy-subs batch videos --prompt_dir=hints --output_dir=subtitles

  3. Check every result against its source video:

    vexy-subs verify subtitles --source_dir=videos

    The command prints the number of verified sets and a summary per video.

docs.title: Translate the result
docs.text:
With an LLM profile configured (see Configuration):

vexy-subs translate subtitles/talk.ass subtitles/talk.pl.ass PROFILE English Polish

The Polish file keeps every cue's timing and the speaker colours. See Translation.

docs.title: Transcription
docs.text: transcribe turns one video into speaker-coloured subtitles. batch does the same for every matching video in a folder. Both need the apple extra.

docs.title: Recognition hints
docs.text:
Hints tell the recogniser which names and terms to expect.

  • --prompt_file takes a non-empty UTF-8 file with the extension .md or .txt.
  • --prompt adds hints inline. If you give both, the inline text comes first.

The whole hint text is passed to Whisper's initial prompt. If the text contains lines that start with Names: or Terms:, only the comma-separated entries on those lines are passed to Whisper instead, so Markdown instructions or programme prose do not reach the recogniser. The same entries also keep their casing when punctuation is restored.

Names: Anna Kowalska, Ben Okafor.
Terms: QuasarAPI, OpenType, Python.
This talk discusses font shaping.

With this file, Whisper receives Anna Kowalska, Ben Okafor, QuasarAPI, OpenType, Python.

A hint is context for recognition. It does not guarantee a replacement, and Whisper's prompt context is finite. With the supported mlx-whisper runtime and condition_on_previous_text=False, the initial prompt applies to the first decoding window; it is not persistent glossary context for a long recording. The receipt records the hint file's name and SHA-256, not its contents.

docs.title: Readable transcripts and model choice
docs.text:
Recognition hints provide spelling context; instructions such as “remove fillers” do not make an ASR model an editor. transcribe already runs punctuation restoration and conservative editorial cleanup after recognition. Use --beautify=False to retain verbatim words, or beautify to revise existing timed captions. Retained word timings are preserved apart from recorded timing repairs; deleted fillers are recorded in the receipt. Immediate repeated phrase starts are removed even when the punctuation model puts a period after an unfinished article (for example, “That’s a. That’s a good lesson”). Complete repeated sentences, questions, pauses and speaker handoffs remain protected. This produces readable captions without free paraphrasing or summarization; punctuation predictions still need editorial review.

A local comparison of Whisper turbo, Parakeet Ultra and Qwen3-ASR 1.7B found that metadata prompts did not improve every excerpt, and an editorial instruction to Qwen left repetitions intact. Recognition speed alone does not establish better technical vocabulary or editorial quality. Whisper remains the supported ASR backend; --asr_model selects a compatible Whisper checkpoint, not another family.

Timing contracts also differ. Whisper supplies word estimates. Parakeet's tested MLX runtime supplies sentence intervals and subword tokens. Qwen's tested MLX runtime supplies audio-chunk bounds, which cannot be treated as sentence timings. Qwen offers a separate forced aligner, but it must be exercised before that route can deliver aligned captions. An alignment estimate is not a native word timestamp.

Implementation references: MLX Whisper, Parakeet MLX, and Qwen3-ASR.

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
--language defaults to en. Pass an empty string, --language="", to let Whisper detect the language.

The default punctuation model supports English, German, French, Italian and Dutch. For other languages, pass a suitable model with --punctuation_model.

docs.title: Diarization back-ends
docs.text:
--diar_backend Behaviour auto (default) Nemotron; switches to cluster when all eight Nemotron slots are filled nemotron Nemotron only; tracks up to eight speakers cluster CPU WeSpeaker embeddings with spectral clustering; estimates the speaker count up to --max_speakers (default 40)

cluster needs the cluster extra. If auto needs to switch and the extra is missing, the run stops with setup guidance.

Nemotron processes the whole recording with one continuous speaker cache, so speaker IDs do not restart partway through. Automatic clustering can merge or split voices, especially in short or noisy turns.

docs.title: Supplied turns
docs.text:
--turns_file skips diarization and uses turns that you have verified. The file is JSON with a turns array and a capacity value:

{
  "capacity": 2,
  "turns": [
    {"start": 0.0, "end": 14.2, "speaker": "speaker_0"},
    {"start": 14.2, "end": 31.8, "speaker": "speaker_1"}
  ]
}

docs.title: How words get a speaker
docs.text:
Each word goes to the speaker whose turns overlap it most. If several speakers overlap a word, it is marked ambiguous in .words.json. Mono audio cannot reliably separate words spoken at the same time.

A word that no turn overlaps takes the nearest turn's speaker if that turn starts or ends within 0.5 seconds of the word's midpoint. Otherwise it stays unassigned and is shown in white.

A word with zero duration takes the speaker of the nearest timed word and is marked ambiguous. It never merges two speakers into one coloured cue.

docs.title: Speaker names
docs.text:
Speaker IDs are anonymous and local to one recording. A programme listing cannot tell which voice belongs to whom. Once you have verified the identities, map IDs to names with --speaker_map:

{"speaker_0": "Presenter", "speaker_1": "Guest"}

Every value must be a non-empty string. The names appear as ASS event names and WebVTT voice names.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
For an input talk.mp4, the outputs go to --output_dir, or beside the video if it is empty.

File Contents talk.ass one style per speaker (Arial 46, outline 3, shadow 1, 1920 × 1080 script resolution); the event name is the speaker label talk.vtt each cue as <v Name><c.speakerN>…</c></v>, with a STYLE rule per speaker class talk.srt each cue wrapped in <font color="#RRGGBB">; some players ignore the tag talk.words.json words: text, start, end, speaker, ambiguous talk.vexy-subs.json settings, hashes, checks and stage information

Use ASS for reliable desktop styling and WebVTT for browser playback.

The first eight speakers get these colours: #7DD3FC, #FDE047, #86EFAC, #FDA4AF, #C4B5FD, #FDBA74, #67E8F9 and #F0ABFC. Further speakers get distinct generated colours. Unassigned words are #FFFFFF.

After writing, all three caption files are parsed again and compared: they must have the same number of cues, the same text, matching times and a speaker style on every cue.

docs.title: The work folder
docs.text:
Model results are saved in talk.work/ in the output folder:

File Stage asr.json recognised words and the raw Whisper result alignment.json words after timestamp repair diarization.json speaker turns punctuation.json punctuated words

Each file is keyed to the input hash and the settings that affect it. If a run fails, the next run reuses every stage whose key still matches. Changing only the beautification settings reuses all four stages.

docs.title: Re-running
docs.text: If the receipt exists, its settings match and every output still has the recorded hash, transcribe prints SKIP talk.mp4: verified and returns the old receipt. If the settings or outputs differ, the run stops; add --force to regenerate. Caption files that have no receipt are never overwritten without --force.

docs.title: Batch processing
docs.text:
vexy-subs batch videos --prompt_dir=hints --output_dir=subtitles
  • --pattern selects the videos; the default is *.mp4.
  • With --prompt_dir, every video must have exactly one hint file named <video stem>.md or <video stem>.txt. This is checked for all videos before any processing starts.
  • Each video runs transcribe in its own process, with a limit of four hours, so models are released between videos.
  • Existing verified outputs are skipped. A failed video does not stop the batch; the failures are reported together at the end.

batch forwards --force, --language, the beautification options, --llm, --strict and --fps. It forwards --diar_backend and --max_speakers only when --diar_backend is not auto.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: Recordings, hint files, personal names, models and run artefacts are your private data. They are excluded from the package's source and wheel builds, which contain only synthetic test fixtures. Nothing is uploaded unless you use translate or the LLM route of beautification.

docs.title: Translation
docs.text:
translate translates an SRT, VTT, ASS or SSA file with any OpenAI-compatible chat model. Every cue keeps its timing, and an ASS input keeps its speaker styles and colours. The extension of the output file chooses its format.

vexy-subs translate SRC DST LLM SOURCE_LANG TARGET_LANG [flags]

Subtitle text is sent to the endpoint you name. Confirm that this is acceptable before you use a remote provider.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# A configured profile, ASS to ASS
vexy-subs translate talk.ass talk.pl.ass cerebras-code English Polish

# An explicit model spec and a glossary, SRT to WebVTT
vexy-subs translate talk.srt talk.de.vtt \
  "gpt-4o::OPENAI_API_KEY::https://api.openai.com/v1" en de --vocab=glossary.json

# Try the "fast" profile first, then "careful"
vexy-subs translate talk.srt talk.fr.srt fast,careful en fr

LLM is a profile name, an explicit model::ENV_KEY::base_url spec, or a comma-separated list of either. See Configuration.

SOURCE_LANG and TARGET_LANG are passed to the model as written, so en and English both work.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --vocab empty JSON glossary of exact term translations --config_file platform config file config.toml to read profiles from --env_file empty .env file to load keys from --chunk_size 40 cues per request --refine True run the second, refining pass --timeout 60 seconds per request --force False replace an existing output

docs.title: How a file is translated
docs.text:
1. The input is parsed. Comment events in ASS files are dropped. A file that contains text but no parsable cue is an error.
  2. Cues are sent in chunks of --chunk_size. Each request contains the glossary and the previous chunk's translation as context.
  3. Each cue travels as numbered JSON, {"id", "text"}, so a cue with several lines stays whole.
  4. The reply must contain exactly the same cue IDs in the same order. A reply that drops, merges or reorders a cue is rejected.
  5. With --refine=True, a second pass rewrites stiff phrasing in the translated chunk, under the same checks.
  6. The translated text is written back into the original cues, so start and end times never change.

docs.title: When a reply is rejected
docs.text:
1. The same model is asked again, with the reason for the rejection.
  2. If it fails again, the next model in the list is tried.
  3. If every model fails, the chunk is split in half and each half is tried again, down to single cues.
  4. If a single cue still fails, the command stops. It never shifts timestamps to make a bad reply fit.

HTTP 401 and 403 errors skip straight to the next model. HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx errors, and network errors, wait and retry. A <think> block before the reply, code fences and prose around the JSON object are tolerated.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
--vocab names a JSON object that maps source terms to their required translations:

{"kerning": "kerning", "typeface": "krój pisma"}

A missing glossary file is an error.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• An existing output needs --force, and the output cannot be the input file.
  • Text in braces, {...}, is read as an ASS override tag when the file is saved, and is lost.
  • To keep speaker colours, translate from ASS to ASS.

docs.title: Migrating from vttrix
docs.text:
vexy-subs translate replaces the retired vttrix package:

vttrix vexy-subs vttrix translate a b llm src dst --vocab=v.json vexy-subs translate a b llm src dst --vocab=v.json from vttrix import ... from vexy_subs import ... [model_providers.*], [profiles.*] in vttrix's config.toml the same tables in the vexy-subs config.toml

Differences: an existing output needs --force, input with text but no cues is an error, and provider discovery matches only upper-case {PREFIX}_API_KEY names with an HTTP(S) endpoint.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with vexy-subs doctor. It shows whether FFmpeg, ffprobe and the optional extras are installed.

docs.title: ModuleNotFoundError for mlx_whisper or mlx_audio
docs.text:
The apple extra is not installed. Reinstall with it:

uv tool install 'vexy-subs[apple,cluster]' --force

The extra needs a Mac with Apple Silicon.

docs.title: Existing output differs; use --force to regenerate
docs.text: A receipt exists for this video, but the settings or the output files differ from it. Add --force to regenerate. Model results in the .work folder are reused where their settings still match.

docs.title: Unmanaged subtitles exist; choose output_dir or --force
docs.text: Caption files with the same name exist but have no receipt. Write elsewhere with --output_dir, or replace them with --force.

docs.title: Existing captions; use --force to render edited words
docs.text: render found existing .srt, .vtt or .ass files at the output stem. Choose another stem or add --force.

docs.title: Eight speaker slots filled; install vexy-subs[cluster] or supply verified turns_file
docs.text: Nemotron found eight speakers, its maximum, and the cluster extra is not installed. Install the extra, use --diar_backend=cluster, or supply verified turns with --turns_file.

docs.title: Require a supported diar_backend and positive max_speakers
docs.text: --diar_backend must be auto, nemotron or cluster, and --max_speakers must be at least 1.

docs.title: speaker_map must be a JSON object mapping IDs to nonempty labels
docs.text: The --speaker_map file must be a JSON object whose values are non-empty strings.

docs.title: prompt_file must be a UTF-8 .md or .txt file or prompt_file is empty
docs.text: Use a non-empty file with the extension .md or .txt.

docs.title: Require exactly one prompt for ...
docs.text: With --prompt_dir, batch needs exactly one hint file per video: <stem>.md or <stem>.txt, not both and not neither.

docs.title: No matching videos
docs.text: batch found no file that matches --pattern (default *.mp4) in the folder.

docs.title: Unresolved subtitle constraints
docs.text: --strict is set and some cues still break a numeric caption rule. Read beautification.audit.violations in the receipt to see which cues. Run without --strict to keep the best available layout.

docs.title: Punctuation is missing or wrong
docs.text: The default punctuation model supports English, German, French, Italian and Dutch. For another language, pass a suitable model with --punctuation_model. Punctuation and diarization are model predictions and still benefit from review.

docs.title: Speakers are merged or split
docs.text: Automatic diarization can merge or split voices, especially in short or noisy turns. diarization.json in the .work folder stores the turns under its data key. Copy that data object, which holds turns and capacity, to a new file, correct the speaker values, and run again with --turns_file and --force.

docs.title: LLM backend requires model and HTTP(S) base_url
docs.text: The LLM route is selected but no model is configured, or the base URL does not start with http:// or https://. Configure [llm] or a profile, or use --backend=local. See Configuration.

docs.title: Unknown LLM profile ... or Provider ... is not configured
docs.text:
The profile or its provider is missing from config.toml. Check with:

vexy-subs llm profiles
vexy-subs llm check PROFILE

docs.title: ... exists; use --force to overwrite (translate)
docs.text: The translation output already exists. Add --force.

docs.title: No subtitle cues could be parsed from ...
docs.text: The input to translate contains text but no recognisable SRT, VTT, ASS or SSA cues.

docs.title: Caption layout lost transcript characters (verify)
docs.text: The captions no longer contain every character of the timed words, usually because a caption file was edited by hand after it was generated. Edit .words.json instead and use render.

docs.title: Changed output: ... (verify)
docs.text: An output file no longer matches the hash in its receipt. Regenerate it, or render it again from edited words.
